description.narrative: The principal objective of the Programmatic Approach is to improve inclusive fiscal and private sector resilience and the scope includes reforms aimed at (a) improving public sector management and sustainability, and (b) enhancing economic and social resilience. The Programmatic Approach comprises two subprograms and the Program is the second subprogram.

Reform area: Public sector management and sustainability improved
Outcome: Consumption tax revenue as share of GDP increased to at least 15.0% of GDP. (FY2015-FY2019 baseline: 13.6% of GDP) Source: Tonga government annual financial statements
Description: To improve public sector management, the cabinet approved for submission to the Legislative Assembly for enactment of the new Public Financial Management Bill 2023 which will: a. improve fiscal management through the codification of fiscal responsibility principles and a requirement to prepare a medium-term fiscal strategy; b. strengthen internal and expenditure controls through the establishment of an internal audit function that reports to an internal audit committee; c. strengthen the management of government liabilities by requiring a debt management strategy, stipulating a numerical limit on the stock of government-guaranteed debt, and setting out the criteria for the granting of future guarantees; and d. support fiscal and debt transparency by providing guidance and deadlines for the online publication of budget documents.

Reform area: Public sector management and sustainability improved

Description: To strengthen fiscal discipline and improve the allocative and operational efficiency of the annual budget, the cabinet approved the PFM Roadmap (2024 -2029), which, among other priorities: a. introduces a new chart of accounts with Government Priority Agenda budget tagging;b b. targets improvements in the quality and coverage of public procurement; c. requires fiscal impact assessments of revenue and expenditure policy changes to be published in the budget documentation; and d. requires including gender equality in the Government Priority Agenda and gender impact assessments of new revenue and expenditure policies to be published in the budget documentation.

Action 2: To improve export competitiveness and support business continuity during crises, the minister for Revenue and Customs has approved and the Ministry of Revenue and Customs commenced implementation of a pilot of the Authorized Economic Operator Secure Export Scheme which reduces trade costs and time to export for perishable goods.
Action 3: To support the development of domestic markets and protect against noncompetitive or unfair practices, the cabinet approved a revised National Policy on Consumer Protection and Competition.
Action 1: To strengthen the social protection system and prepare for a timely, efficient, and gender-sensitive disaster response, the cabinet approved:
i. an Adaptive Social Protection Framework to ensure timely and efficient social assistance support during emergencies; and ii. the establishment of a National Social Registry to collate household data disaggregated by sex and vulnerability status across agencies and improve the targeting of social protection programs.
Action 2: To strengthen social resilience and preparedness in response to impending hazards, the cabinet submitted the Communications (Amendment) Bill to the Legislative Assembly, which enables the dissemination of disaster early warning information through the cell broadcasting system.
Action 3: To further improve export competitiveness, and reduce barriers to the movement of goods, the cabinet has approved the mainstreaming of the Authorized Economic Operator Secure Export Scheme, including the adoption of processes to onboard additional exporters and the streamlining of additional cross-border processes.
Action 4: To codify the Competition and Consumer Protection Policy approved in subprogram 1, the cabinet approved the submission of a new Consumer Protection Bill to the Legislative Assembly.
